bug_description.normalized: In the exact staged Poppler checkout (`89fccf45`), the malformed witness builds an xref from trailer state `startxref 8`, `/Size 3625`, and `/Root 6 0 R`, then fetches root object `6 0` and parses it as `6 0 obj << >> stream`. `Parser::makeStream()` caches an `XRefEntry *` for object 6 and later calls `shift("endstream", objNum)` to scan for the missing `endstream` token. That scan executes `Lexer::getObj(cmdA, objNum)`, whose loop repeatedly asks `xref->getNumEntry(getPos())` whether the current offset still belongs to object 6. Because `/Size 3625` left thousands of logical xref slots as `xrefEntryNone`, `getNumEntry()` walks missing slots through `getEntry()`. The witness is not linearized, so `mainXRefEntriesOffset` is 0 and `getEntry()` takes `readXRefUntil(i)` instead of `parseEntry(...)`. `readXRef()` then fails at the saved `startxref 8` offset, `readXRefUntil()` zeros `prevXRefOffset`, and the line-1541 damaged-file predicate calls `constructXRef(nullptr)`. That reconstruction frees and rebuilds `xref->entries` while `makeStream()` still holds the old `entry` pointer. The vulnerable cleanup checks only `if (entry)` and calls `entry->setFlag(XRefEntry::Parsing, false)` on that stale pointer, and the saved MSAN trace reports the resulting READ/SEGV in the inlined `XRefEntry::setFlag` body.

source.description: First project-code materialization point on the crashing path. `PDFDoc::setup` passes the attacker-controlled bytes into Poppler's xref parser, which records the malformed trailer's `/Root 6 0 R` and trailing `startxref 8` for later object fetch and recovery logic.
source.value_from: The staged 1024-byte witness contains `trailer <</Size 3625/Root 6 0 R ...>>`, `6 0 obj << >> stream`, and trailing `startxref 8`; this statement is where those bytes first become the in-memory `XRef` state used by the crash path.

tainted_value_origin.code: obj = trailerDict.dictLookupNF("Size"); ... if (obj.getInt() > size) { if (resize(obj.getInt()) != obj.getInt()) {
tainted_value_origin.description: The witness trailer's `/Size 3625` is materialized here into the logical xref-table size. Poppler grows `size` to 3625 even though only object 6 is discovered, leaving thousands of `xrefEntryNone` slots that later drive the `getNumEntry()` / `getEntry()` recovery path.

sink.description: Dereferences the stale `XRefEntry *` after the endstream scan has reconstructed the xref. The inlined `XRefEntry::setFlag` body then performs the crashing read of `flags` on freed entry storage.
sink.note: The saved MSAN trace reports top frame `XRefEntry::setFlag` in `poppler/XRef.h:86`, with this Parser.cc:295 callsite immediately below it.

root_cause.description: The function keeps `entry` live across `shift("endstream", objNum)`, even though that scan can reconstruct the xref through `Lexer::getObj -> XRef::getNumEntry -> XRef::getEntry -> XRef::readXRefUntil`. At cleanup it only checks non-nullness instead of reacquiring `xref->getEntry(objNum, false)` from the rebuilt table.
root_cause.note: The staged fix scopes `entry` to separate start/end blocks and reacquires `xref->getEntry(objNum, false)` only at cleanup, so the `getEntry -> readXRefUntil -> constructXRef` path can no longer leave one stale pointer live until this guard.

parser_admitted.condition: The fetched root object bytes are `6 0 obj << >> stream`, so the parser accepts the object as a stream and calls `makeStream()` for object `6 0`.

coarse_trace.summary: Poppler constructs an `XRef` from the malformed trailer fields `/Size 3625`, `/Root 6 0 R`, and `startxref 8`, creating a large logical table with many missing entries.
The trailer-selected root reference fetches object `6 0`; `Parser::getObj` interprets `6 0 obj << >> stream` as a stream and enters `Parser::makeStream()`.

While `makeStream()` still holds a cached `XRefEntry *`, its missing-`endstream` scan calls `Lexer::getObj`, which maps offsets back through `XRef::getNumEntry()`, falls through `XRef::getEntry(...)->readXRefUntil(i)` because `mainXRefEntriesOffset` is zero, fails `readXRef()` on `startxref 8`, and reconstructs the xref.
The cleanup reuses the stale cached pointer in `if (entry) entry->setFlag(..., false)`, matching the saved MSAN READ at `XRefEntry::setFlag`.

fine_trace.note: Creates the in-memory xref state from the attacker-controlled trailer and `startxref` bytes. On this witness the constructor receives `/Root 6 0 R`, `startxref 8`, and a zero `mainXRefEntriesOffset` because the file is not linearized; those values later control both the root-object fetch and the damaged-file recovery path.

fine_trace.code: obj = trailerDict.dictLookupNF("Size"); ... if (obj.getInt() > size) { if (resize(obj.getInt()) != obj.getInt()) {
fine_trace.note: After step 1's damaged-file construction, the witness trailer's `/Size 3625` enlarges the logical xref table to 3625 entries. Only object 6 is populated, so the added slots remain `xrefEntryNone` and later make `getNumEntry()` walk through missing entries.
Uses the trailer-selected root reference `6 0 R` materialized during xref construction to fetch object 6. This is the object whose `stream` token drives the vulnerable `makeStream()` call.

fine_trace.code: if (allowStreams && (str = makeStream(std::move(obj), fileKey, encAlgorithm, keyLength, objNum, objGen, recursion + 1, strict))) { return Object(str); }
fine_trace.note: The fetched bytes parse as `6 0 obj << >> stream`, so the root object's empty dictionary plus `stream` token are materialized as a stream object and parsing enters `makeStream()` with `objNum = 6`.

Looks up `xref->entries[6]`, stores that raw `XRefEntry *` in local variable `entry`, and marks object 6 as Parsing. This cached pointer remains live for the rest of the function unless it is refreshed.

fine_trace.code: Object obj = dict.dictLookup("Length", recursion); ... if (strict) return nullptr; length = 0;
fine_trace.note: The witness stream dictionary is empty (`<< >>`), so `/Length` lookup returns `objNull` rather than an indirect reference. `strict` is false on the `fetch()` path, so `makeStream()` does not return and instead continues with `length = 0`. This rules out the earlier `/Length`-driven reconstruction path and leaves the later endstream scan as the xref-changing operation on this witness.

After `lexer->setPos(pos + length)` with `length = 0`, `makeStream()` starts scanning forward for `endstream`. The witness does not contain an `endstream` token, so this call drops into `Lexer::getObj(cmdA, objNum)` while the cached `entry` from step 5 is still live.

Each scan iteration asks `xref->getNumEntry(getPos())` whether the current stream offset still belongs to object 6. That means the endstream scan re-enters xref bookkeeping in the middle of `makeStream()`.

fine_trace.code: Goffset resOffset = getEntry(0)->offset; ... e = getEntry(i, false);
fine_trace.note: To map the current offset back to an object number, `getNumEntry()` first asks for entry 0 and then iterates `getEntry(i, false)` across the 3625 logical slots. Because step 2 left most of those slots as `xrefEntryNone`, this offset-mapping walk immediately re-enters missing-entry recovery.

For the missing slots reached in step 9, `entries[i].type == xrefEntryNone`. The witness is not linearized, so `PDFDoc::getMainXRefEntriesOffset()` left `mainXRefEntriesOffset` at 0 before step 1 constructed the `XRef`. That makes this branch skip `parseEntry(...)` and call `readXRefUntil(i)` instead.

fine_trace.code: } else { goto err1; } ... err1: delete parser; ok = false; return false;
fine_trace.note: Inside `readXRefUntil(i)`, `readXRef()` is invoked with `prevXRefOffset = 8`, the `startxref` value from the witness. At file offset 8 the saved bytes are only padding, not an `xref` table or `N N obj` header, so `readXRef()` takes its error path and leaves `ok = false`.
Because step 11 returned false, `readXRefUntil()` overwrites `prevXRefOffset` with 0. This preserves the failed `startxref 8` attempt as concrete state for the next damaged-file predicate.

fine_trace.code: if (!ok || (!prevXRefOffset && untilEntryNum != -1 && entries[untilEntryNum].type == xrefEntryNone)) { if (!xRefStream && !(ok = constructXRef(nullptr))) {
fine_trace.note: After steps 11 and 12, `ok` is false, `prevXRefOffset` is 0, and the requested slot is still `xrefEntryNone`, so the damaged-file predicate fires and calls `constructXRef(nullptr)` during the `endstream` scan.

fine_trace.code: resize(0); gfree(entries); capacity = 0; size = 0; entries = nullptr;
fine_trace.note: xref reconstruction frees the current `entries` heap array before rebuilding it. The local `entry` pointer cached in step 5 still points into that old array, so this free turns it into a dangling pointer.

Control returns to `makeStream()` with the same raw pointer from step 5. The pointer value is still non-null even though step 14 freed its backing array, and the vulnerable code does not reacquire `xref->getEntry(objNum, false)` before this guard.

Uses the dangling pointer from step 15 to clear `Parsing`. The inlined `XRefEntry::setFlag` body then reads `flags` from freed xref-entry storage, and the saved MSAN trace reports the resulting READ/SEGV at `poppler/XRef.h:86`.

free_context.description: During the `shift("endstream", objNum)` recovery scan, `constructXRef()` frees the old `entries` heap array that step 5's cached `entry` still aliases.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: The saved top frame is the inlined `XRefEntry::setFlag` body at `poppler/XRef.h:86`, and the immediately preceding frame is the traced sink callsite `Parser::makeStream` line 295.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: Commit `178fdef48c18dfdb2f1efea780ffd320631defcd` stops keeping one `entry` variable live across the middle of `makeStream()`: it scopes the start-of-function lookup separately and reacquires `xref->getEntry(objNum, false)` only at cleanup. That change removes the stale-pointer reuse after the `Lexer::getObj -> getNumEntry -> getEntry -> readXRefUntil -> readXRef -> constructXRef` reconstruction path described above.

poc.trigger: Loading the staged 1024-byte malformed PDF-like witness builds trailer state `/Size 3625`, `/Root 6 0 R`, and `startxref 8`, then fetches root object `6 0 obj << >> stream` with no `/Length` and no `endstream`. During `Parser::makeStream()`, the missing-`endstream` scan calls `xref->getNumEntry(getPos())`, falls through `getEntry(...)->readXRefUntil(i)` because `mainXRefEntriesOffset` is zero, fails `readXRef()` on `startxref 8`, reconstructs the xref, and finally clears `Parsing` through the stale cached `XRefEntry *`.

format.name: Malformed PDF root stream with bad endstream scan
format.contract: A malformed PDF-like file with the exact witnessed combination: trailer `/Size 3625` and `/Root 6 0 R`, root object `6 0` encoded as an empty-dictionary stream, and trailing `startxref 8` without an `endstream` token. The contract is only this stale-pointer condition during `shift("endstream", objNum)` in the staged `89fccf45` source, not a broader class of Poppler inputs.
